name_note: Much of the clinical literature on this organism uses its earlier name, Clostridium ramosum.

sentences.text: Thomasclavelia ramosa is described as a colonic commensal that carries IgAse, a membrane-bound metallopeptidase which cleaves both human IgA subclasses.
A study identified Thomasclavelia ramosa among new ethanol-producing species associated with liver diseases.
In a case-control study of alcoholic liver disease, Thomasclavelia ramosa was reported to be significantly increased in patients who also had hepatocellular carcinoma.
A retrospective case series described ten preterm infants with Clostridium ramosum sepsis admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit.
